findings.title: T12's signed-move panel states the minuscule identities on every built node, where they are false (D4 node 2, the acceptance example) or their stated failure is false (B3 node 1)
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:918-934 (snippet signedPanel; the panel is drawn whenever rep.built, line 1087); route /tools/rep/?z=1&g=D4&k=2. M8's challenge b10 sends the reader to E6 node 2, where the same false text shows.
findings.claim: The panel prints, with no condition, 'Firing node k permutes the positions: its matrix is Ek + Fk + Pk ... The group element exp(Ek) exp(−Fk) exp(Ek) is Ek − Fk + Pk: the same matrix with one sign changed in each pair.' On every node that is not minuscule it adds 'the moves of numbers 2 or more are missing from E and F, so the signed matrix is no longer the move with signs.' The first two sentences are false wherever the orbit has a number of size 2 or more at node k. The third is false wherever it has none.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.18 states both identities 'in a minuscule representation', and verify.py section 14 checks them on the 18 minuscule records only. On D4 node 2 at k = 2, the firing matrix S_2 is a permutation, but E2+F2+P2^0 has zero columns at ±alpha_2. Likewise (I+E2)(I−F2)(I+E2) = exp(E2)exp(−F2)exp(E2) is invertible, but E2−F2+P2^0 is singular. On B3 node 1 at k = 1, every number at node 1 is −1, 0 or 1, so S_1 = E1+F1+P1^0 and the signed matrix is the move with signs.
findings.observed: D4 node 2: the panel text as quoted, beside 'Signed: E2 − F2 + P2' with empty columns at (1,−2,1,1) and (−1,2,−1,−1). B3 node 1: the panel says 'no longer the move with signs', but the engine's matrices satisfy both identities at node 1. Oracle over the 509 (node, k) states of the 85 built non-minuscule nodes: the first two sentences are false in 450 states and the third in the other 59 (B_n node 1, C_n node n, B2 node 1 at k = node).

notes: SPEC versus mathematics, for the owner: the 2.16 table cell 'The diagram ... always changes' (copied by M8 beat 8 and not-quiver-mutation) is false at a vertex with no arrow, for example the one-vertex quiver, where Fomin-Zelevinsky mutation leaves the quiver as it is. It is true at every vertex of a connected quiver with at least two vertices.

SPEC 2.7 opens with '"Finite type" means one of the boards of section 2.8'. The site never gives the reader this definition: its glossary and M3 define finite by spectral radius below 2, and the engine's requireFinite accepts boards in several pieces. A refutation of P5-RT-09-05 can cite 2.7. The finding rests on the site's own definition and on the M8 repair that added 'connected'. This touches the held F11 wording.
